script_nghe: Excuse me, how do I get to the museum? … Take the number twenty-eight bus — sorry, no, the twenty-eight doesn’t run today. Take the eighty-two. … The eighty-two. Where do I get off? … After four stops. Then turn left and walk straight on. The museum is opposite a large church, you can’t miss it. … Is it far from the bus stop? … No, about six minutes on foot.

> **The city’s new metro**
> 
> The first metro line opened last year after eight years of construction. It runs from the northern suburbs to the city centre, a distance of eighteen kilometres, with fourteen stations. A single ticket costs 15,000 dong, and a monthly pass costs 200,000.
> 
> In the first six months, around 30,000 people used the line every day — far fewer than the 100,000 the city expected. Officials say the main problem is that most stations are not near where people live, so passengers still need a motorbike or bus to reach them. A second line, which will cross the first at Central Station, is planned for 2029.

**Multiple choice (6–8):** chọn A, B hoặc C.

1. The metro line took
   A. six months to build B. eight years to build C. eighteen years to build
1. Passenger numbers were
   A. higher than expected B. exactly as expected C. lower than expected
1. According to officials, the main problem is
   A. the ticket price B. the location of stations C. the number of stations

**Hoàn thành câu (9–11):**
9. The line has ____________ stations.
10. A monthly pass costs ____________ dong.
11. The second line will cross the first at ____________.

writing.de_tom_tat: Viết 60–70 từ chỉ đường từ nhà bạn đến địa điểm gần nhất.
writing.bai_mau: Go out of my building and turn left. Walk straight on for about two hundred metres until you reach the traffic lights. Cross the road and take the second turning on your right. The market is on your left, opposite a small pharmacy. It takes about five minutes on foot. If you pass a big bank, you have gone too far.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Go out · turn left · Walk straight on · Cross the road · take the second turning — động từ nguyên mẫu đứng đầu câu, không có chủ ngữ. Đúng hết.
out of the building · on your right · on your left · opposite · on foot.
the second turning — dùng số thứ tự, không phải “the two turning”.

dang_hoc: Chỉ đường dùng câu mệnh lệnh: bỏ chủ ngữ, động từ nguyên mẫu đứng đầu.
Bộ từ chỉ đường cần thuộc: go straight on · turn left/right · take the first/second turning · cross · go past · opposite · next to.
on foot (đi bộ) · by bus/car/bike — hai giới từ khác nhau.
loi_thuong_gap: ❌ You go straight → ✅ Go straight (mệnh lệnh thì bỏ You)
❌ take the two turning → ✅ take the second turning

speaking.de_tom_tat: How do you usually travel around your city? / Is public transport good where you live? / Do you prefer walking or taking a bus?

cau_tra_loi.hoi: How do you usually travel around your city?
cau_tra_loi.mau: By motorbike, like most people here. It's the quickest way to get around, especially in narrow streets.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: “like most people here” — thêm bối cảnh văn hoá làm câu trả lời có chiều sâu.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Is public transport good where you live?
cau_tra_loi.mau: It's improving, but it's still limited. We have buses and one metro line now, though the buses can be slow in rush hour.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: “It's improving, but…” — cách nói cân bằng, hay hơn nhiều so với “yes” hoặc “no” đơn thuần.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Do you prefer walking or taking a bus? Why?
cau_tra_loi.mau: Walking, if it's not too hot. It's healthier and I don't have to wait. But in the rainy season I'd rather take a bus.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: “I'd rather…” = tôi thà… — cấu trúc nâng điểm, sau I'd rather là động từ nguyên mẫu.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Đủ, có so sánh hai chiều.
vehicle /ˈviːəkl/ — chữ h câm. motorbike nhấn âm đầu: MO-tor-bike.

meo_noi: “get around” = đi lại trong thành phố — cụm rất tự nhiên.
“I'd rather + V nguyên mẫu” (không có to): I'd rather take a bus.
